name.text: Points inside on or outside a circle

questiontext.text:
The locus of points \({@r@}\) units from \(C({@C[1]@}, {@C[2]@})\) is a circle. For each point, decide where it is.

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
A point is on the circle when its distance from \(C\) is exactly \({@r@}\), inside when it is less and outside when it is more. By Pythagoras the square of the distance is \(\Delta x^2 + \Delta y^2\), where \(\Delta x\) and \(\Delta y\) are the moves across and up from \(C\). Compare it with \({@r@}^2 = {@r^2@}\), so that nothing is rounded.

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\): \({@dx[1]@}^2 + {@dy[1]@}^2 = {@d2[1]@}\), [[if test="is(cats[1]=1)"]]less than \({@r^2@}\), so inside[[elif test="is(cats[1]=2)"]]equal to \({@r^2@}\), so on the circle[[else]]more than \({@r^2@}\), so outside[[/if]].

  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\): \({@dx[2]@}^2 + {@dy[2]@}^2 = {@d2[2]@}\), [[if test="is(cats[2]=1)"]]less than \({@r^2@}\), so inside[[elif test="is(cats[2]=2)"]]equal to \({@r^2@}\), so on the circle[[else]]more than \({@r^2@}\), so outside[[/if]].

  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\): \({@dx[3]@}^2 + {@dy[3]@}^2 = {@d2[3]@}\), [[if test="is(cats[3]=1)"]]less than \({@r^2@}\), so inside[[elif test="is(cats[3]=2)"]]equal to \({@r^2@}\), so on the circle[[else]]more than \({@r^2@}\), so outside[[/if]].

  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\): \({@dx[4]@}^2 + {@dy[4]@}^2 = {@d2[4]@}\), [[if test="is(cats[4]=1)"]]less than \({@r^2@}\), so inside[[elif test="is(cats[4]=2)"]]equal to \({@r^2@}\), so on the circle[[else]]more than \({@r^2@}\), so outside[[/if]].

questiondescription.text:
Loci: points inside, on or outside a circle locus

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.3: Decide whether a point is inside, on or outside the locus of points a fixed distance from a point, by Pythagoras.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 7, Section A, questions A2 and A6 of Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Core 1 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2004: the inside, on or outside test by Pythagoras, as a classification with trap points; new circles and points, none of C1's.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).
